name: Make a simple wooden box
blurb: The classic first project: it demands square cuts, accurate joints, a fitted bottom and a finish. Everything you get wrong is visible, which is exactly why it teaches so well.
gear: Timber — pine or poplar to start
A square, and a finish such as oil or wax
steps: Design it on paper with real dimensions, and produce a cutting list including the thickness of every piece.
Cut the four sides, keeping opposite pairs identical in length — this matters far more than hitting the exact nominal size.
Cut your chosen corner joint: rebates for a first box, finger joints or dovetails if you are ambitious.
Cut a groove for the base so the bottom floats in it rather than being nailed on.
Dry-fit everything, check the diagonals are equal, then glue and clamp square.
Sand progressively through the grits and apply a simple oil or wax finish, then fit a lid or hinges if you want them.
tips: Equal diagonals mean a square box. Check while the glue is wet, when you can still fix it.
Sand up through the grits without skipping, and always with the grain on the final passes.
proof: A box that sits flat, closes properly, has tight corners and a finish you are happy to give away.
